# N21: A switched-off module’s addresses say so, and who can switch it on; the read-back before switching Reviews off counts what stays

A check of the Reviews module ([its section](../README.md#journeys-and-checks)): not a journey with steps a person takes, but a script that opens pages and reports what is wrong (Faro’s `evals/notes/21-switched-off.cjs`). A rebuild proves the same by hand or with its own script: every failure below must not happen. Each is in the script’s words; {…} is what it measured.

## What it checks

a switched-off module's addresses (FT2, docs/design/feature-toggles/spec.md sections 3, 4.2 and 9). run({ open, url }) returns a list of failures. As Amara, an admin, on a computer: switching Reviews off first reads back what stays, and its counts are the workspace's (the rule switchOffReadBack: reviews not ended or removed, what was said or marked in them, the open next steps and questions raised in one); then, with every installed module switched off, each of their routes (from each module.json) is Page not found with “{Name} is switched off in {workspace}. An admin can switch it on in Workspace, Features.”, a link for an admin, and its Help link (if any) doesn't open the module's hidden article; Help lists none of their articles, Reviews' article address says it is off, and What's new still lists their releases (Lane, 14 Nov). For Rhea, who isn't an admin, the line is words, not a link, and Features offers her no switch (setModule refuses her too: src/domain/actions.ts, its unit test).

## Where it looks

- 1440 × 900, as amara, at `/workspace/features`

A width of 390 is a phone, 1440 (or 1280) a desktop; the address is in the demo on Thursday 5 November 2026 unless it names another day.
